q: Consider the Preamble: 1-It was held in 1960 not to be part of the Constitution. 2-That view was revised in 1973. 3-It has been amended twice. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: It has been amended once, by the 1976 amendment inserting three words.
why: The two judgments are correctly stated; only the count of amendments is wrong, and one amendment is the figure to retain.
trapnote: The Preamble has been amended exactly once. Any other count is the planted defect.

q: The date appearing in the Preamble is:
options: 26 January 1950, being the date of commencement
26 November 1949, being the date of commencement
26 November 1949, being the date of adoption
26 January 1950, being the date of adoption
expl: The Preamble records adoption; commencement followed on 26 January 1950 and is not in the text.
why: All four options pair a real date with a real event, so only the correct pairing distinguishes them.
trapnote: Two dates, two events, one document. Only the adoption date appears in the Preamble.

q: Consider the words inserted in the Preamble in 1976: 1-Socialist. 2-Secular. 3-Federal. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Socialist and Secular were inserted, together with Integrity; Federal was not.
why: Federal is attractive because India is described as federal in character, but the word does not appear in the Preamble at all.
trapnote: The third inserted word is Integrity, not Federal. The Preamble never uses the word federal.

q: A person voluntarily acquires the citizenship of a foreign State and then claims to retain Indian citizenship. Which statement is correct?
options: Indian citizenship continues, the overseas status conferring full dual citizenship
Indian citizenship ceases, the Constitution barring voluntary dual allegiance
Indian citizenship continues until a competent authority formally cancels it
Indian citizenship ceases only where the foreign State is a neighbouring country
expl: Voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship terminates Indian citizenship.
why: The overseas citizen status is widely misdescribed as dual citizenship, which is what makes the second option persuasive.
trapnote: Overseas citizenship is a registered status with limited rights. It is not a second citizenship.

q: Consider the citizenship provisions at commencement: 1-One deals with migration from Pakistan to India. 2-One deals with return to India under a permit after migrating to Pakistan. 3-One deals with registration by persons of Indian origin residing abroad. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Three separate provisions cover migration in, return under permit, and registration from abroad.
why: The distinguishing feature between the first two is the direction of travel, and the word permit belongs only to the second.
trapnote: Direction of travel separates the migration provisions. The word permit appears in only one of them.

q: Which statement correctly describes the expression 'the State' for the purposes of fundamental rights?
options: It includes every body performing a function of public importance, without more
It excludes local authorities, which are governed by a separate Part
It includes local authorities and other authorities under governmental control
It includes the judiciary in the exercise of its adjudicatory functions
expl: Local and other authorities are included; control rather than public importance is the test.
why: The fourth option is the classic half-truth: the judiciary counts in its administrative capacity, not its adjudicatory one.
trapnote: Control is the test, not public importance. And the judiciary counts only in its administrative role.

q: A body is held not to be 'the State'. Consider: 1-No Supreme Court petition lies for fundamental rights. 2-No High Court writ lies against it at all. 3-A High Court writ may lie for its public functions. Correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The Supreme Court route closes; the High Court route can remain open for public functions.
why: The second and third statements are direct opposites, so the candidate must know which of the two survives the finding.
trapnote: The High Court writ power runs against any person or authority and does not depend on this definition.

q: A pre-Constitution law is inconsistent with a fundamental right. Which statement is correct?
options: It is void in its entirety from the date the Constitution commenced
It is void to the extent of the inconsistency and may revive if that is removed
It remains valid until Parliament repeals or amends the provision
It is void only after a court has expressly declared it to be so
expl: Severability limits the voidness and the eclipse doctrine permits revival.
why: The fourth option confuses the effect of a declaration with the source of invalidity, which arises from the Constitution itself.
trapnote: Two doctrines operate together here: severability limits the damage, eclipse permits revival.

q: Consider: 1-A constitutional amendment is 'law' for the purpose of the bar on laws abridging fundamental rights. 2-An amendment may nevertheless be struck down for damaging the basic structure. 3-The provision excluding amendments was inserted in 1971. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Amendments were expressly taken outside the bar in 1971, but the basic structure check remains.
why: The check did not disappear; it moved from one doctrine to another, which is the point the set is built around.
trapnote: The bar was removed and a different limit took its place. The check moved rather than vanished.

q: A municipality demolishes a shop without notice and without any law authorising it. Which statement is correct?
options: A local authority is not the State, the remedy lying only in civil proceedings
A local authority is the State, but municipal action is immune from rights review
A local authority is the State, and the action fails for want of a fair procedure
A local authority is the State only where it receives grants from the government
expl: Local authorities are expressly included, and action without law or procedure fails.
why: The fourth option invents a funding condition, borrowing the language of the control test and misapplying it.
trapnote: Local authorities are named expressly. No funding or control inquiry is needed for them.

q: A custom excludes a community from a village well. Which statement is correct?
options: Custom lies outside the bar, which reaches only enacted legislation
Custom lies outside the bar, but is separately void as an unreasonable practice
Custom is within the bar only where a court has previously recognised it
Custom having the force of law is within the bar, and the custom falls
expl: The definition of law expressly includes custom and usage having the force of law.
why: The second option reflects the intuitive but wrong assumption that only statutes can be tested.
trapnote: Custom and usage having the force of law are expressly covered. The bar is not confined to statutes.

q: On the 1955 citizenship statute and its 2019 amendment: 1-Both rest on Parliament's plenary power. 2-The amendment uses a cut-off of 31 December 2014. 3-It applies uniformly to all areas of India. Correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Areas under the Sixth Schedule and inner line permit regimes are excluded.
why: The third statement is the defect and is easily missed because the exclusion is geographical rather than substantive.
trapnote: Check for geographical carve-outs. A statute can be general in subject and limited in territory.

q: An institution receives deep and pervasive government funding and control, but is registered as a private society. Which statement is correct?
options: It may be the State if the control test is satisfied on the facts
It cannot be the State, registration as a society being conclusive
It is the State automatically once any government funding is received
It may be the State only if a statute expressly so declares
expl: Form of registration is not conclusive; deep and pervasive control can bring a body within the definition.
why: The third option converts a multi-factor test into a single automatic trigger, which is the commonest overstatement here.
trapnote: The control test is cumulative and factual. Neither registration nor any single factor is conclusive.

q: Consider the Preamble's objectives: 1-Justice is described as social, economic and political. 2-Liberty covers thought, expression, belief, faith and worship. 3-Equality is described as of status and of opportunity. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: All three descriptions match the text of the Preamble.
why: Sets in which every item is accurate test verification; the temptation is to assume that one item must be planted.
trapnote: Learn the four objectives with their qualifying words. They are asked as exact phrases.

q: A claim is made that because the Preamble is part of the Constitution, the three words inserted in 1976 are invalid. Which statement is correct?
options: The claim succeeds: the Preamble being part, it is beyond the amending power
The claim fails: the Preamble is not part of the Constitution at all
The claim succeeds: only the original text of the Preamble has legal force
The claim fails: the Preamble is part of the Constitution and is amendable
expl: Being part of the Constitution makes it amendable, subject to the basic structure.
why: The claim inverts the consequence of the 1973 holding, treating inclusion as immunity rather than as amenability.
trapnote: Being part of the Constitution brings a provision within the amending power, not outside it.

q: Consider: 1-India has single citizenship. 2-Every State prescribes its own additional citizenship requirements. 3-Domicile requirements for employment in a State may be prescribed only by Parliament. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Citizenship is single and uniform; residence requirements for posts rest with Parliament.
why: The second statement is the planted defect and is attractive because States do prescribe local requirements in other contexts.
trapnote: Single citizenship is absolute. Local preferences in employment arise from other provisions entirely.

q: An aided university expels a student without a hearing and pleads that it is a private body. Which statement is correct?
options: It may be the State on the control test, and a fair hearing is in any event required
It is not the State, and no hearing requirement arises in a private institution
It is the State solely because it receives aid from the government
It is the State only if it was established by a statute of the legislature
expl: Aid alone is not decisive, but deep control can be; and the duty to hear can arise independently.
why: The fourth option states a sufficient condition as though it were a necessary one, which is a frequent logical trap.
trapnote: Distinguish sufficient from necessary conditions. A statutory body is the State; not only statutory bodies are.

q: Consider the doctrine of eclipse: 1-It applies to pre-Constitution laws. 2-The eclipsed law is dormant rather than dead. 3-It applies equally to post-Constitution laws against citizens. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The doctrine operates on pre-Constitution laws; post-Constitution laws stand on a different footing.
why: The third statement is the defect and turns on a distinction that is easy to state and easy to forget.
trapnote: Pre and post Constitution laws are treated differently under the bar. The doctrines are not interchangeable.

q: Which statement about the amendment of the Preamble is correct?
options: It may be amended only by a law ratified by half the State legislatures
It may not be amended at all, being a declaration of the people's will
It may be amended only where the amendment enlarges an existing objective
It may be amended under the general amending power, subject to the basic structure
expl: The Preamble is amendable like any other part, subject to the basic structure limit.
why: The second option imports the federal ratification requirement, which does not attach to the Preamble.
trapnote: Ratification attaches to specified federal provisions only. The Preamble is not among them.

q: A migrant produces documents of birth, parentage and continuous residence. An officer asserts authority to confer citizenship on that basis. Which statement is correct?
options: Status flows from the officer's satisfaction once the documents are found genuine
Status flows from the Constitution and the citizenship statute, not from a police verification
Status flows from the State government's order on a police recommendation
Status flows from inclusion in the electoral roll of the constituency concerned
expl: Conferral of status rests with the statutory authority; verification is not conferral.
why: The fourth option is attractive because electoral rolls are widely treated as proof of status; they are indicative only.
trapnote: Verification is not conferral, and a roll entry is evidence rather than title.
